definition: A storage method that pumps water into an elevated reservoir during low-price periods and releases it through a hydroelectric turbine to regenerate electricity when needed, operating as a closed-loop version of a conventional hydro plant.
core_idea: Pumped hydro stores energy as gravitational potential energy by moving water uphill during the storage phase and letting it flow back down through a turbine during generation; with sufficiently large upper and lower reservoirs it can store substantial energy for an extended period.
key_points: Water is pumped from a lower storage facility to an elevated reservoir during the storage phase.
Released water drives a hydroelectric turbine to regenerate electricity when power is needed.
The concept is similar to a conventional river-fed hydro plant but operates as a closed system pumping water back above a dam rather than relying on river flow.
Sufficiently large reservoirs at the top and bottom of the facility allow storage of a large quantity of energy for an extended period.
